{
  "candidate_rtl": "module ticket_machine #(
    parameter ON  = 1'b1,
    parameter OFF = 1'b0
) (
    input  clk, clear, ten, twenty,
    output reg ready, dispense, return_sig, bill
);

    // Binary state encoding preserves the original state transitions.
    localparam [2:0] RDY    = 3'd0,
                     BILL10 = 3'd1,
                     BILL20 = 3'd2,
                     BILL30 = 3'd3,
                     DISP   = 3'd4,
                     RTN    = 3'd5;

    reg [2:0] State, NextState;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (clear)
            State <= RDY;
        else
            State <= NextState;
    end

    always @* begin
        ready      = OFF;
        dispense   = OFF;
        return_sig = OFF;
        bill       = OFF;

        case (State)
            RDY: begin
                ready = ON;
            end

            BILL10,
            BILL20,
            BILL30: begin
                bill = ON;
            end

            DISP: begin
                dispense = ON;
            end

            RTN: begin
                return_sig = ON;
            end

            default: begin
            end
        endcase
    end

    always @* begin
        case (State)
            RDY: begin
                if (ten)
                    NextState = BILL10;
                else if (twenty)
                    NextState = BILL20;
                else
                    NextState = RDY;
            end

            BILL10: begin
                if (ten)
                    NextState = BILL20;
                else if (twenty)
                    NextState = BILL30;
                else
                    NextState = BILL10;
            end

            BILL20: begin
                if (ten)
                    NextState = BILL30;
                else if (twenty)
                    NextState = DISP;
                else
                    NextState = BILL20;
            end

            BILL30: begin
                if (ten)
                    NextState = DISP;
                else if (twenty)
                    NextState = RTN;
                else
                    NextState = BILL30;
            end

            DISP,
            RTN: begin
                NextState = RDY;
            end

            default: begin
                NextState = RDY;
            end
        endcase
    end

endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The original implementation uses a six-bit one-hot state register and separate state decoders for both outputs and next-state selection. This increases state-register load and decode/mux logic on the input-to-state setup paths.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the six-bit one-hot encoding with a three-bit binary encoding, merge equivalent bill-producing states in the output decoder, and merge the identical DISP/RTN transition behavior. The sequential block, clear polarity, enable behavior, state transition priority, and output latency remain unchanged.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Potential setup improvement from reduced state width and less duplicated decode logic, especially on paths through the state register and output decode. The gain is expected but unmeasured; EDA timing analysis is required before claiming improvement.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "The binary state register uses three flops instead of six and should generally reduce mapped area. Binary decoding can have different logic depth than one-hot decoding, so timing and area must be checked against the fixed area cap. No additional sequential elements are introduced.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the original module name, parameters and defaults, ports, widths, signedness, single positive-edge clock, active-high synchronous clear, and output latency. ten retains priority over twenty when both are asserted. DISP and RTN still return to RDY on the following clock, bill remains asserted in BILL10/BILL20/BILL30, and arbitrary later clear assertions still force RDY on the active clock edge. Invalid binary states retain the original default behavior: all outputs OFF and next state RDY. Verification should compare against the frozen original after the fixed one-cycle reset and warmup contract."
}
